en.title: Orange-Roasted Lamb Chops
en.text: Main ingredient Lamb chops Seasoning and vegetables Bay leaves, chili powder, ground white pepper and ground black pepper Ground fennel, ground cumin, chicken bouillon powder, salt, MSG and sugar Starch, light soy sauce, sesame oil and Shiyitang barbecue marinade Orange (seeds removed), onion and garlic Method Prepare and marinate. Mince the garlic and slice the onion. Remove the orange seeds, slice the orange and squeeze out the juice. Soak the garlic and onion in the juice. Cut the lamb into strips, mix well with the seasonings and marinate for at least two hours. Roast. Line an oven tray or air fryer basket with the onion and orange slices. Roast at 180°C for 12 minutes, then turn the chops over. Raise the temperature to 200°C and cook for another 3–5 minutes. Look for a golden surface while the meat is still juicy. There is no need to brush the lamb with oil. Start with the fat side up so the fat can melt and run down over the meat.

zh.title: 橙香烤羊排
zh.text: 橙香烤羊排 主料 羊排 配料 香叶 辣椒粉 白胡椒粉 黑胡椒（粉） 小茴香（粉） 孜然（粉） 鸡精 食盐 味精 白糖 生粉 生抽酱油 香油 世一堂烧烤腌料 橙子（去籽） 洋葱 大蒜 做法 1.备料与腌制： 大蒜切成末，洋葱切条，橙子去籽后切片挤出来汁并加入大蒜末和洋葱浸泡，上面配料与切成条状后的羊排抓匀，腌制至少2小时。 2.烤制： 烤箱烤盘或空气炸锅底面铺洋葱、橙子片，180度烤12分钟后翻面，提升至200度烤3-5分钟（不要把瘦肉烤柴，表面金黄色但保证肉质不干，饱满时即可） ps： 羊排不用刷油，第一轮烤制时应将肥肉面冲上，方便油脂向下滴落覆盖整块肉。

en.title: This Is What Sichuan Chili Chicken Should Taste Like!
en.text: Sichuan Chili Chicken These amounts are for about 1 kg of chicken, or two to three chicken legs. Ingredients Chicken legs: 2–3 (about 1 kg). You can also add wings or feet. MSG and sugar: half a spoon each (about 2–3 g each) Chinese black vinegar: half a spoon (about 1–2 g) Ginger and garlic: about 30 g each, finely chopped Shallots or spring onions: 3–5 (about 20 g), finely chopped Dried Qixing chilies: one handful (about 30 g), for heat. Other hot chilies work too. Dried bullet chilies: one handful (about 30 g), for their bright red color. Other small red chilies work too. Dried lantern chilies: one handful (about 30 g), cut in half. They add aroma and a little heat. Green Sichuan peppercorns: two handfuls (about 30 g) Fried peanuts: two handfuls (about 50 g) Toasted white sesame seeds: 2–3 spoons (about 10 g) Sichuan pepper oil: one spoon (about 5 g) Numbing Sichuan pepper oil: two spoons (about 10 g) Prepared rapeseed oil: 3–4 spoons (about 20 g) Cut and marinate the chicken Cut the chicken into 1–2 cm pieces. Pat them dry with kitchen paper or shake off the extra liquid in a strainer. Small, dry pieces take on the flavor more easily and have a better texture. Mix the chicken with one spoon of salt, half a spoon of ground pepper, two spoons of cooking wine and two spoons of light soy sauce. Mix by hand until the pieces feel slightly sticky. Stir in one egg yolk for a golden color, then mix in two spoons of dry starch to help make the outside crisp and keep the inside tender. Finally, mix in 3–4 spoons of oil to help the pieces separate when frying. Fry the chicken twice Pour enough oil into a wok to make a layer about 4–5 cm deep. Heat it over high heat. When a little smoke appears, add the chicken and quickly separate the pieces. Turn the heat down to medium and fry for about one minute, until the pieces hold their shape. Lift them out and remove any crumbs from the oil. Heat the oil again over high heat. When it starts to smoke lightly, turn off the heat and fry the chicken a second time for 20–30 seconds. Lift it out and let the oil drain. The outside should now be golden and crisp. Stir-fry and serve Heat rapeseed oil in the wok over high heat. When the oil starts to move, turn the heat down to medium. Fry the ginger, garlic, shallots, green Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies for about 30 seconds, until they smell fragrant. Add the chicken, turn the heat down to low and stir-fry for two minutes. Add MSG and sugar, then pour the vinegar around the edge of the wok. Add the fried peanuts, toasted sesame seeds, Sichuan pepper oil and sesame oil. Toss everything a few more times over low heat and serve.

zh.title: 这才叫辣子鸡！
zh.text: 这才叫辣子鸡！ 四川辣子鸡正宗做法 本篇调料比例参考鸡肉重量为1000g（约2-3个鸡腿） 准备材料 鸡腿肉：2-3个（约1000g） （也可另加鸡翅、鸡爪，因人而异） 味精：半勺（约2-3g） 白糖：半勺（约2-3g） 香醋：半勺（约1-2g） 生姜：1块（约30g） 切成姜末 大蒜：半头（约30g） 切成蒜末 香葱头：3-5个（约20g） 切成葱末 （可用小葱代替） 七星椒（干）：1把（约30g）（主要提供辣味，可用够辣的其他辣椒代替） 子弹头朝天椒（干）：1把（约30g）（主要提供色相，颜色红亮，可用普通朝天椒代替） 灯笼椒（干）：1把（约30g） 对半切开（主要提供香味，且辣度仅微辣） 青花椒：2把（约30g） 油酥花生米：2把（约50g） 炒熟的白芝麻：2-3勺（约10g） 花椒油：1勺（约5g） 麻椒油：2勺（约10g） 熟菜籽油：3-4勺（约20g） 鸡肉切块 将鲜鸡翅、鸡腿肉斩切成1-2cm小块 然后用厨房用纸把血水擦干，或放在漏勺里反复颠控至无水。 (鸡肉适当地剁小点能方便入味，减少多余的水份可以提升鸡肉的口感) 腌制鸡肉 将鸡肉置入容器，加入： 盐：1勺 胡椒粉：半勺 料酒：2勺 生抽酱油：2勺 将所有调料抓匀，抓拌至鸡肉感觉有些粘手。 然后加入 鸡蛋黄：1个 搅拌均匀。（加蛋黄的作用是让鸡肉颜色能金黄亮丽） 蛋黄搅拌均匀后再加入 干淀粉：2勺 搅拌均匀。（加干淀粉能防止鸡肉纤维变老，外酥里嫩） 最后加入 油：3-4勺 搅拌均匀备用。（加入油的目的是防止鸡肉下锅炸的时候粘在一起，自动散开） 炸鸡块 锅中倒油（约4-5cm高） ，大火 烧至油温 7成热 （油表面出现薄弱的油烟时，油温为7成热） ，将鸡肉下入油锅并快速把鸡肉块打散，转 中火 炸 1分钟 左右把鸡肉炸至定型后用漏勺捞出，再用漏网再锅中 捞出杂质 （防止杂质炸糊后附着在鸡肉上）。 因为油温会被鸡肉冷却，所以转 **大火* 将油温烧至 *8成热*** *（油表面冒青烟时，油温为8成热） 后 关火 ，并下入鸡块复炸 20-30秒 后捞出并 控油 备用。（鸡块因为又复炸一遍，此刻表皮变得金黄酥脆 😋） 炝锅 锅中倒入 菜籽油 ，大火 将油烧至 6成热 （油内开始翻滚时油温为6成热） 后转 中火 ，加入 姜末、蒜末 、 香葱头 、 青花椒 、 干辣椒 ，大约 爆炒30秒 将辅料爆香。 翻炒 下入 鸡肉块 ，转 小火 后 翻炒2分钟 ，此时辅料的辣味、香味融入已经到鸡肉里。 加入 味精 、 白糖 （用于提鲜） ，从锅边淋入 香醋 ，倒入 油酥花生米 、 炒熟的芝麻 、 花椒油 、 芝麻油 。 最后在 小火 下反复 翻炒 几次，将所有调料 炒匀 后即可出锅装盘。

en.title: My First English Diary
en.text: Hi! This is my first diary entry in English. I study English every day, but I still have a long way to go. If I want to go abroad, I need to improve. I have been learning English for a year, but I have spent more time playing games on my Switch than studying. Now I only have four months to prepare for IELTS. Come on, I can do this! I need to stop spending so much time on games. If I get a good score, I can play more later. This feels like a good start. I will use this diary to record my progress in English. I believe I can do it!

zh.title: 我的第一篇英语日记
zh.text: 你好！这是我的第一篇英语日记。 我每天都学英语，但水平还有很大的提升空间。如果我想出国，就必须把英语学得更好。我已经学了一年，可我花在 Switch 游戏上的时间比学习的时间还多。 现在我只剩四个月准备雅思。加油，我能做到！别再把那么多时间花在游戏上了。等我考出好成绩，以后就有更多时间玩了。 这是一个不错的开始。我会在这里记录自己的英语学习进度。加油，我相信自己！

en.title: Action Is Better Than Preparation
en.text: There is an old saying in The Doctrine of the Mean: “With preparation, things succeed. Without it, they fail.” But too much preparation can become a way to put things off. When I want to practice writing, I might tell myself I need a nice pen, a beautiful notebook and a comfortable chair. Even after I get all three, I can still find new things I think I need before I start. Preparing well can help me do a better job. Putting things off, however, keeps me from taking the first step. Good running shoes can make a run more comfortable, and good headphones can make music sound better. Once I start running or listening, I care less about the equipment and more about what I am doing. If the task were an exam, good preparation would give me extra points. The only way to pass would be to take the exam. Starting lets me enjoy the process, see what I can achieve and learn from what happens next.

zh.title: 行动胜于准备
zh.text: 「行动」胜于「准备」 俗话说『凡事预则立不预则废』，但在某种意义上，过度的准备反而成为了拖延症的一种表征。 以写作为例，当我需要练习写作时，可能会觉得非要购买一支精美的笔、一本漂亮的笔记本和一把舒适的椅子，然后才能开始写作。然而这种准备还不足够，因为即使一切看似准备就绪，拖延的人仍然会为「开始行动」设想更多的「伪需求」来做所谓的「准备」。 拖延症患者其实没有弄明白一个事实：万全的准备是为了让事情变得「尽善尽美」，而无限的拖延却会让人永远无法迈出「开始」的第一步。一双好跑鞋可以提升跑步体验，一副HiFi耳机可以使音乐更动听。然而，跑步的核心在于运动本身，音乐的核心在于音乐本身。当我们进入「进行中」的状态时，那些所谓的「准备」的重要性会逐渐被淡忘。 如果我们将需要做的事情看作是一场「考试」，那么「万全的准备」只是「加分项」，而真正「及格」的关键在于「行动起来」。只有通过行动，我们才能真正体验到过程的乐趣和成果的成就，不要畏惧迈出第一步，勇敢地挑战未知的可能性，才能获得真正的成长和进步。

en.title: How to Keep Your Energy Up
en.text: I usually sleep less than eight hours. Last night, for example, I went to bed at 1 a.m. and woke up at 7 a.m. That gave me only six hours of sleep. I need a clear head to do things well, but when I am tired, even learning something new feels harder. That is why good sleep matters to me. First, I try to go to bed earlier. When I use my phone, I often lose track of time. Some apps are so entertaining that I keep using them long after I planned to stop. It feels as if someone is stealing my attention and selling it for a few coins. Second, I take a short break when I feel tired. I sometimes set an alarm and take a 15-minute nap. For me, that small break can make it easier to focus for the next couple of hours. Third, I try not to eat too much at once. I often feel sleepy after a large meal, especially one with a lot of meat or grains. When my stomach feels lighter, I find it easier to stay alert. I do better work when I have enough energy. Good habits help me get more done without wearing myself out.

zh.title: 如何保持充沛的精力
zh.text: 我总是睡不到八小时。比如昨晚一点才睡，今天七点就醒了，只睡了六个小时。我做事情需要头脑清醒，可我常常做不到。累的时候，连学东西都学不好，所以睡个好觉很重要。 首先，别太晚睡。我用手机时经常忘了时间。有些应用太有趣，让我兴奋起来停不下来。感觉就像有人偷走了我的注意力，然后只卖了几个小钱。 其次，累了就休息一下。设个十五分钟左右的闹钟，小睡一会儿。对我来说，这点时间换来大约两个小时的好精神，很划算。 第三，也是我认为最重要的，别吃得太多。我的感觉是，胃就像一台机器，忙着消化时，我做事没那么有效率。尤其吃了肉或谷物之后，我容易犯困。肚子比较空的时候，我就没那么困。 做好事情需要充足的精力。养成好习惯，才能事半功倍。

en.title: A Perfectionist’s Mug
en.text: I have a special mug from Nintendo, the video game company. It has six black hearts, three on each side. You might recognize them if you have played The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. When you pour hot water into the mug, the hearts turn red. This is the fourth one I have owned. I paid about 200 yuan for it. I sold the first mug because there were a few black spots on the side. I kept noticing them every time I drank from it. After about a month, the perfectionist in me decided to sell it. About six months later, I wanted another one. I could not explain why. I just liked it. But the second mug had a bigger problem. The hearts on the first mug had turned red, while the hearts on the new one turned light red, almost pink. I could not live with that, so I ordered a third mug. When it arrived, I felt hopeless. It had the same problem. I wondered if the second and third mugs had been made that year and the first one the year before. Maybe I could get the color I wanted by finding an older one. I finally bought the fourth mug secondhand. It has its own flaws, but I do not want to spend more time and energy looking for a better one. I can keep my dream mug in mind and look for it again after I reach my main goal. As a perfectionist, I find it hard to accept flaws. Still, I remind myself that getting things done matters more than getting them perfect. I have more important things to finish now. The smaller things can wait, and by then I might have forgotten about them anyway.

zh.title: 完美主义者的杯子
zh.text: 「完美主义者的杯子」 我有一个特别的杯子，这个杯子是由任天堂公司（Nintendo Corporation）生产的，是一家电子游戏公司。 为什么这个杯子特别呢？ 杯子的壁上有六个黑色的心形图案，每边有三个。如果你玩过一款名为《塞尔达传说：荒野之息》的游戏，你就会知道它。当你将热水倒入杯子时，这些心形图案的颜色会从黑色变为红色。 顺便说一下，我手上的这个杯子是我第四个杯子，我花了大约两百元买到它。 我的第一个杯子我卖掉了，因为它有一些瑕疵，比如杯壁上有一些黑点。然后，当我用这个杯子喝水时，我总是担心那些斑点。大约一个月后，作为一个完美主义者，我决定把它卖掉。 过了很久，大约半年后，我突然又想要另一个。我无法解释这种欲望，也许只是因为我喜欢它，就是这么简单。不幸的是，当我收到第二个杯子时，它有一个更大的瑕疵。我的第一个杯子的心形图案是红色的，但第二个杯子的心形图案是浅红色的，几乎像粉红色！ 我无法忍受，所以我又买了一个新的。但是当我收到第三个杯子时，我感到绝望… 我无法相信我所看到的，第三个杯子也有同样的问题。所以我思考了一会儿，我觉得第二个和第三个是今年生产的，而第一个是去年生产的，因此它们的颜色不同。如果我买一个去年生产的杯子，我就可以得到我想要的一个很棒的杯子。 最后，我在二手市场上买到了第四个杯子，说实话，第四个杯子并不完美，但我不想再花更多的时间和精力去找更好的杯子。我记得自己的目标是得到一个完美的杯子，在实现主要目标之前，等待时机再买我梦寐以求的杯子。 作为一个完美主义者，接受有瑕疵的东西太困难了，但我总是告诉自己：“生活需要去做，而不是追求完美。” 尽管我想把每件事都做得完美，但我必须完成更重要的事情，那些不重要的事情可以在将来完成。我也觉得，也许在将来，我会忘记这件事。

en.title: So That’s How I Lost My Rubik’s Cube
en.text: I never understood how I lost my Rubik’s Cube. Today I finally worked it out: I did not lose it. It walked away on its own. I had never found a cube that felt right, so one day I took a chance and bought this one. I still remember the joy of picking it up for the first time. It felt just right. For more than a month, I played with it day and night. When it was out of reach, it felt like something was missing. Later, more little things came along to entertain me. They covered that first joy like layers of snow on a mountain. I used to think the cube had vanished in some accident. In fact, I had slowly stopped paying attention to the toy I once took everywhere. I would play with it when I felt like it and set it aside when I did not. Maybe that lack of care is what made it disappear. “What is the opposite of love?” “Is it not loving someone? Is it hate?” “No. The opposite of love is forgetting.”

zh.title: 原来魔方是这么丢的啊！
zh.text: 原来魔方是这么丢的啊！ 一直不明白我的魔方到底是怎么丢的，直到今天才想明白，它没丢，是它自己走了。 在还没有一个和我心意的魔方时，一狠心一闭眼就买下了它。 第一次接触到这个魔方的瞬间，那种欣喜，那种对味儿的感觉，即便是现在似乎还能回忆的起。 刚拿到手后那一个多月，我真是喜欢的不得了！是天天把玩，没日没夜不离手，似乎一会碰不到就像缺了点什么一样。 后来，能取悦我的小玩意越来越多，它们像是高山上的雪，一层一层地将我最初那种喜悦覆盖得严严实实。 我一直以为，此时魔方不翼而飞是出自某次意外，但事实上是因为我慢慢地开始变得不再去关注那个魔方，不去在意那个曾一直寸步不离的「玩具」。 正因如此，让它消失的，不是随手一丢的偶然遗失，而是我的那种“想玩它就摆弄两下，不想玩就搁置一边”的单方面「不在乎」吧… 「爱的反义词是什么？」 「是“不爱”，是“恨”么！」 「不，爱的反义词是“遗忘”」

en.title: Even the Most Beautiful Dream Is Still a Dream
en.text: Perhaps life has been a little rough lately. I was watching The Hongwu Cases when Ouyang Lun placed first in the imperial exam. It reminded me of my own three exams. I had placed second, third and first, in that order. In the end, I walked away from all of it. It left me with a bitter feeling. I kept thinking, “If only I had done this instead, then things might be different now.” It reminded me of a Mid-Autumn Festival episode of My Own Swordsman. Everyone at the inn was watching the moon, sighing about the choices they could have made. They sounded just like me. But even if I had chosen differently, who can say I would not have regrets again? How could anyone know the right choice without being able to see the whole picture? Maybe the best thing I can do now is make a better life for myself. Then, when I look back, I might think, “I am glad I did not take that civil service job. Otherwise, I might never have had the life I have now.” Even the most beautiful dream is still a dream. What is in front of you is real. Do not leave your cup empty under the moon. Raise it to the people you are lucky enough to meet. Wishing for fish by the water will get me less than going home and making a net. I have made my choice. Now I want to focus on it and do my best, so I can look back without regret.

zh.title: 幻境再美终是梦，珍惜眼前始为真
zh.text: 幻境再美终是梦，珍惜眼前始为真 可能是现在过的多少有些凄惨，刚才看《洪武大案》的时候，演到欧阳论中举第一甲第一名时，才回想到自己三次考试分别中了榜眼、探花、状元，可惜最后放弃了啊。 心里面很不是滋味，总觉得当初“如果不是、而是、就如何如何……” 突然记起来《武林外传》里面有一集中秋赏月，同福客栈的各位唉声叹气，他们和我现在一模一样，总是在感叹“如果当初不是，而是，那现在就如何如何”。 但真的当初做了不同的选择，谁又能保证不会再一次后悔呢？谁又能在没有上帝视角的情况下做出绝对正确的选择呢？ 也许我现在最应该做的就是让自己活得更好，这样一来当再次回忆之前的事情时，才能去想“还好当初没去上岸，否则我现在还过不上这样的日子”。 幻境再美终是梦,珍惜眼前始为真。 莫使金樽空对月,举杯幸会有缘人。 与其临渊羡鱼，不如退而结网。我现在只是希望目前做了抉择后，集中一点登峰造极，努力着可以让自己不再后悔….

en.title: Some Thoughts on Living Forever
en.text: I have been thinking about this. What if, one day, we could freeze a brain and upload or download a mind? Imagine putting your mind into a robot and freezing your brain for 30 years. Suppose freezing it for that long costs the brain five years of its useful life. The robot could live in your place and store its memories. When the 30 years are over, you could download those memories and repeat the process. Would that count as living longer? Of course, the robot might just run away when its time is up. Those 30 years would really be a set of data, like a long novel. You would give up some of your brain’s life for a set of experiences you could call your own. Perhaps people would find it simpler to feed new experiences straight into the brain. That brings me to a harder question: what makes me who I am? I used to think the answer was my brain. A new arm would not make me a different person. Even if my whole body were replaced, I would still feel like myself. But imagine copying my mind into a new, empty brain. The person in front of me looks like me and has the same memories, unconscious thoughts, DNA and brain cells. Yet I am still standing here. Even if the original me died a second later, the other person would still be a new copy of me. I used to guess that the brain might have a limit of roughly 120 to 150 years. If it has a limit, being able to print and replace every other organ would only go so far. Uploading a saved copy of my mind to a new body and then removing the original would still be a form of copying. What I want from living forever is to keep living myself. I can imagine two ways forward. One would be to repair or regrow brain cells and tissue so the original brain keeps working. The other would be to connect a new brain to the old one, let the mind move slowly to the new brain, then remove the old one and put the new brain in a new body. Both ideas would require medical technology far beyond what I can take for granted. These may be clumsy ideas. But if people could first extend the life of the brain, they might have more time to answer the other questions.

zh.title: 对于实现永生的一些思路
zh.text: 对于实现永生的一些思路 我在想一个事情。 如果有一天科技进步到大脑可以冷冻，并且意识可以上传和下载，那是不是可以将意识上传到机器人身上，然后冷冻大脑（冷冻若是有损耗，好比冷冻30年的话 ，大脑寿命可能会缩减5年），冷冻一个最具性价比的时常，好比30年吧，这30年一直由机器人来替你生活，并且这30年的经历会记忆到机器人的储存中，30年过后，将这30年的意识下载到你的脑中，然后开始下一轮的轮回，是不是相当于延长寿命了？ 但也可能30年到期之后 机器人就跑了…… 不过这30年最后实质上是一段数据，就像一部长篇小说，你牺牲大脑的寿命，得到的是一段属于自己的经历。 或许以后人们会逐渐意识到不如直接给大脑不断地输入各种经历才是最具备性价比的人生吧。 那么，人的本质，或者本体是什么？ 之前一直认为人的本质是大脑，因为胳膊没了安装一个胳膊还是自己，哪怕全身瘫痪，最后换了全身，我还是我。 但是，如果把我的意识传输到另一个全新的空白大脑之后，我面前的那个人造人和我长得一样，拥有跟我相同的记忆、潜意识，同样的DNA和神经元，但是我还是不是我？哪怕下一秒把我直接火化成灰，世界上只存在一个复制的我，那么这个人造人也不是我，只能说是复制了的一个新的我，而不是原本的我。 大脑是有寿命的，大概是120-150年吧，所以即便全身器官都可以打印和换新，人类也不能达到永生，又或者制作一个全新的包含大脑的人体把自己的意识上传给新的身体，实际上也只能通过复制的方式上传，因为整个过程一定是将自己的意识保存，在新的身体上上传，而后删除原本自己的意识。 所以我觉得这个不算是永生，因为永生的目的不是为了让这个世界上有一个和我一样的意识替我存在，而是由我自己来存在。 因此我有两个思路，通过这两个方式来达到真正的永生： 第一种，至少在具备打印所有器官，能人造器官与自己的各个器官、大脑相连接且相匹配的医疗科技水平下，通过逆转或者再生脑细胞、脑组织来让大脑的寿命无限延长； 第二种，仍然需要具备第一种那种医疗科技水平下，制作一个全新的健康的大脑作为容器，直接安在原本的大脑上，让新的和老的大脑做一个连接，然后人的意识慢慢的搬家到新的大脑容器上，再切掉老的已经没有意识的大脑，最后将那个新的大脑安装到人造身体上，实现生命的延续。 这两种可能是两个笨方法，但是至少能在很多难题没有搞懂的情况下，暂时把生命延长下来，其他的事情相信在人类大脑寿命延长之后，终究能有答案的。

en.title: I Finally Found the Loki Coin!
en.text: It was hard to find! One day I came across a Tieba post from someone looking for an Asgardian Loki coin. As a Loki fan, I knew I had to find one too. I started checking Xianyu, Amazon and eBay every day. That was in early 2021, and the post was already from late 2014. If people could not find it years earlier, what chance did I have? After more than a year of searching, I finally found it on Xianyu. The seller was clearing out some things and asked just 39 yuan. Even if she had asked for 930, I might have thought about it and said yes! When the coin arrived, it felt heavy in my hand. The design has raised details and smooth lines. On the front is Tom Hiddleston’s Loki, right down to his hairline. The letters L O K I sit above his head. I do not know why those four letters get to me so much, but I could not stop looking at them. The back shows Loki’s helmet. It feels a little different from the grand portrait on the front, but it suits him. I could hardly believe that something I had dreamed about was now in my hands. Then I lost it a few days ago. I turned the whole house upside down and finally found it in the trash. Maybe it is like the rose on the little planet in The Little Prince. I put so much feeling into finding the coin that the search became part of what I love about it.

zh.title: 我终于淘到了LOKI硬币！
zh.text: 我终于淘到了LOKI硬币！ 实属不易！ 曾偶然之间在贴吧看见一篇帖子：《求这款LOKI阿斯加德钱币洛基硬币T^T》，作为一个LOKI迷，顷刻之间产生了一种即便求之不得也势在必得的疯魔心理，从此之后便走上了每天一刷闲鱼、Amazon、eBay的不归路。 那时是2021年初，而那篇帖子是2014年末发布的，内容都是在求这枚硬币，试想……7年前的人都寻不得这枚硬币，何况6年后呢？ 终于！一年多的坚持不懈之下，总算在闲鱼找到了这枚硬币的踪迹，有一个卖家为了践行断舍离，愿意出掉这枚硬币，仅卖39元！要知道，哪怕她卖930元，我也会犹豫之后接受啊！ 等收到这枚硬币的时候，它是那么的厚重，突出的纹理，流畅的线条，正面是抖森饰演的洛基头像，如此生动，甚至发际线都完美地上移了，顶部浮雕刻着“L O K I”，我也不知道这几个字有什么魔力，让我神魂颠倒，如痴如醉。背面是洛基的头盔，多少有点和正面的气派格格不入，但却很好地迎合了洛基这个角色的派头。 我实在不敢相信，曾经梦到的东西如今能在现实之中看得见摸得着！ 前几天还不小心丢了……给我心疼的呀！把家里翻了个底朝天，终于在垃圾桶里找到了它…… 不过，可能是因为它在我眼里，现在就像是『孤单星球的玫瑰』一样吧，为其投入了太多的感情，所以硬币只是个载体，而我的爱，源自它的来之不易吧……

en.title: What a New Phone Taught Me
en.text: When I got the iPhone 13, I felt fairly calm. I thought it was a gift I did not really need. What mattered more was what it made me realize. The way we show care can be completely different from the way someone else hopes to receive it. I think she does not care when she spends the day on her phone, hardly talks to me and only asks for a shoulder or leg massage. She thinks I do not care because I spend all day making good food but rush her through the shops as if we are in a funeral procession. In the end, we are speaking different languages.

zh.title: 新手机礼物给我的警示
zh.text: 新手机礼物给我的警示 其实收到iPhone13的时候，我的内心是平静的，只是觉得没必要…… 真正有价值的是它带给我的警示： 每个人对别人好方式，以及期待别人对自己好的方式，是完全隔绝互不相通的。 我觉得她天天玩手机不搭理我，只想着我给她捏肩捶腿，这是不在乎我的表现。 她觉得我天天只知道做好吃的，逛街的时候就像在赶尸，这是不在乎她的表现。 其实，语言不通罢了。

en.title: The Long Road to the Civil Service Exam
en.text: I decided to take the civil service exam because I wanted to escape the pressure to compete. Somewhere along the way I lost sight of who I was, then began to find myself again. I do not know when I started wanting only a quiet, comfortable life. I told myself I was looking for a stable place where I could settle down and study, but I could not fool myself for long. I was just looking for something that would give my life a sense of purpose. Even a quiet life can be hard to get. Just look at how competitive the civil service exam has become. I need to grow up and move forward. Maybe I should get a job working with Java, gain experience at a big company, go abroad, build a good life and study biomechanical engineering. Maybe that is how I can do something meaningful with my life. Or maybe there is another road. I do not know yet. The road is so long I cannot see where it ends.

zh.title: 漫漫公考路
zh.text: 漫漫公考路 考公务员是为了不卷，所以才考公务员。 不过在这个过程中，逐渐迷失自我，而又找回了自我。 不知道从什么时候开始，我开始变得“平凡”，只想过上安乐的生活，麻痹自己，欺骗自己，告诉自己是找一个安稳的环境后好能静下心来学习，但自己欺骗不了自己，我只是想找个什么事情让自己有点“活着的意义”。 然而，平凡的生活也不是所有人都有资格能享受的到的，你看现在考公务员，多卷？ 赶紧成长吧，要么赶紧入行Java然后大公司历练、出国、过上美好的生活、学习生物机械工程，最终实现我的人生价值。 要么… 我也不知道，路太长，看不到尽头。

en.title: The Loki Coin I Found in the Trash
en.text: I had been looking for my Loki coin all day. How did it end up in the trash? I closed my eyes and tried to remember. At around three in the morning, I had been under the covers, turning the coin between the fingers of my left hand. That helped me narrow my search to the area around the bed. I looked under the bed, along the sides and in every gap. Then I tried the trash can. I shone a bright flashlight into the bottom and saw a flash of light. Without that flash, I might never have held that rare coin again. Did the car somehow knock it into the trash the last time we drove? Did she throw it away to get back at me because she was angry about having to drive tired? Or did some other version of me throw it away while I was too exhausted to remember? Maybe it was just a coincidence.

zh.title: 垃圾桶里找到的LOKI硬币
zh.text: 垃圾桶里找到的LOKI硬币 很好奇为什么找了一天的LOKI硬币会出现在垃圾桶里。 通过闭目冥想不断追忆，终于回忆起来凌晨三点多的时候好似有那么一会，左手在被窝里面通过中指、食指、大拇指来摆玩硬币，最终才把范围锁定在卧室大床的附近。 床底也找了，床沿床缝隙都找遍了，抱着试一试的态度翻了一下垃圾桶，用强光手电筒照射垃圾桶的底端，突然反射出一道亮光，也许没有这道光，我可能这辈子也触碰不到这枚绝版硬币了。 那么问题是，究竟是最晚开车的时候，车身刚好把硬币刮到垃圾桶里的，还是她因为疲劳驾驶愤愤不平以此来报复，又或是精神疲惫之后另一个“我”在我不省人事的时候偷偷扔掉的呢？ 可能只是个巧合吧……

en.title: The Drawing Showdown Ends in a Tie 😂
en.text: Round One When: Early 2018 Where: IKEA One of us was studying PHP and the other was studying English. There was a squirrel on a bookmark. We looked at each other and smiled. Result: a tie! Round Two When: 2 March 2020 Where: One of us was in Bijiang Mingyuan and the other was in Meixi. We brought up our last contest. Cat was not happy with the result, so she came back with a drawing of a cat. We shared a smile even though we were far apart. Result: another tie! To be continued.

zh.title: 美术战争之旗鼓相当😂
zh.text: 美术战争之旗鼓相当😂 第一回合 日期：2018年 年初 地点：宜家家居 事件：一个学PHP一个学英语，书签上有只松鼠，两人相视一笑…… 比赛结果：平局！ 第二回合 日期：2020年3月2日 地点：分别在碧江名苑、美溪 事件：突然提起上次比赛，猫子略有不服，故祭出一张猫咪图，两人相隔千里会心一笑…… 比赛结果：平局！ 未完待续

en.title: Success Depends on Making Progress
en.text: No matter how smart you are or how quickly you learn, you will never reach the finish line if you keep changing your goal or stopping and starting. The road always feels long. Sometimes the end feels out of reach. At this speed, you really will never get there. Can the Milky Way keep bothering people for a hundred years? And could I ever go back and live through 2016 again in this same body?

zh.title: 进度即是成败
zh.text: 进度即是成败 不论一个人是否聪明是否有悟性，但如果目标总是变动，又或走走停停，那一定无法抵达终点。 路总是很远，甚至不可能抵达！ 真要按照现在的速度，你就真的不可能抵达了！ 银河能否烦人百年？ 还有，可能否用同样的躯体去重游一次2016年？
